text:
Alex: seeing a bunch of console tiles blanking out on prod for multiple customers, getting 500s from analytics API. dashboard/metrics returns blank tiles :confused:
Alex: first noticed ~10:05 UTC, affecting orgs 'acme-inc' and 'beta-saas'
Jordan: thanks for the ping, can you paste the exact request you saw?
Alex: curl -i "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/analytics/metrics?org=acme-inc&range=1h" -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx'
Alex: response: HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error
Alex: body: {"error":"internal_server_error","id":"req_01Fz8YJ4"} and some tiles are timing out (504) in the console too
Maria: SRE here, I saw duplicate alerts for analytics-api latency spike at 10:04 UTC. pulling logs now.
SRE-Bot: alert: analytics-api.p95_latency > 500ms (10:04:22 UTC)
Lucas: can you check whether dedicated routing or a specific region is affected? any model-serving spikes?
Jordan: not seeing model-serving overload in infra graphs, only analytics-api spikes
Nina: I've got the initial error trace from the analytics service logs:
Nina: "ERROR [analytics.handler] request_id=req_01Fz8YJ4 failed to compute timeseries: upstream=timeseries-db timeout after 120s"
Jordan: timeseries-db had a short GC pause earlier, but shouldn't cause 500s across multiple orgs; might be a request fanout bug
Alex: repro steps for support: 1) login -> console -> open Project -> Overview -> wait for tiles 2) some tiles show spinner then blank 3) network tab shows POST https://api.redwood.ai/internal/metrics 500
Alex: attaching HAR excerpt: POST /internal/metrics 500 0.23s id=req_01Fz8YJ4
Maria: thanks. Jordan, can you grep for req_01Fz8YJ4 across services?
Jordan: grep returned traces: analytics-api -> query-coordinator -> timeseries-proxy -> timeseries-db. timeseries-proxy returned 504 to query-coordinator at 10:04:21
Jordan: query-coordinator then returned 500 to analytics-api due to unhandled upstream errors
Lucas: sounds like analytics-api isn't handling 504s gracefully, needs fallback and better error mapping
Nina: stack excerpt from query-coordinator:
Nina: "Caused by: java.net.SocketTimeoutException: Read timed out\tat com.timeseries.client.HttpClient.execute(HttpClient.java:213)"
Alex: customers are pinging support: "graphs not loading since 10:05" and some billing dashboards unaffected, so scope seems limited to analytics service
Jordan: I'm opening a hotfix: map upstream 504 -> 502/503 with retry for idempotent queries, and return a stable error payload so console can show a helpful msg instead of blank tiles
Maria: rolling back the recent timeseries-proxy config change from this morning to see if it helps (it reduced connection pool but may have been too aggressive)
SRE-Bot: deploy rollback started: config/timeseries-proxy@deploy-2025-10-01-09:58 UTC
Jordan: ops: can you run the failing query locally against staging timeseries to reproduce? Alex, do you have sample body?
Alex: sample payload (redacted): {"org":"acme-inc","metrics":[{"name":"latency","agg":"p95"}],"range":"1h"}
Lucas: I ran that against staging and got a 200 with data, so likely prod-only (config/pool size or network tiering)
Maria: prod timeseries-proxy had connection_pool.max=8 after the change, increasing to 50 now. applying patch
Maria: patch applied, restarting timeseries-proxy pods (3 pods) :hourglass_flowing_sand:
SRE-Bot: pod-restart: timeseries-proxy-0 terminated -> timeseries-proxy-0 restarted (10:12:40 UTC)
Jordan: after restart I'm seeing reduced 5xxs, some tiles starting to populate for acme-inc
Alex: confirmed, acme-inc tiles back for me at 10:13:05. beta-saas still flaky
Nina: additional metric: timeseries-proxy connection_errors peaked at 10:04 (x284) then dropped after restart
Lucas: putting in a postmortem action: add circuit breaker in query-coordinator to short-circuit upstream timeouts and return 503 with guidance to console
Jordan: also adding a console change: if analytics API returns 5xx, show a "Data temporarily unavailable" card instead of blank tile. I'll make a small UX patch
Alex: can we notify affected customers? I'll draft a support note and patch the incident status page
Alex: draft to customers: "We're investigating an analytics dashboard outage affecting graph tiles between 10:04-10:13 UTC. Some graphs may have been blank or timed out. We rolled a configuration change and restarted components; metrics are returning to normal. Follow-up details will be posted."
Maria: we'll keep monitoring for 30m. if errors resurface, escalate to infra on-call @Lucas
Lucas: ack, monitoring dashboard link: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/analytics/summary?org=internal
Nina: follow-up: we'll add more robust retry/backoff for timeseries proxy client, and improve logging to include query hash for faster traces
Jordan: created ticket INFRA-873: "Handle timeseries upstream timeouts gracefully + add circuit breaker" and DASH-422: "Console: show placeholder on analytics 5xx"
Alex: thanks team :heart: need to update the support thread and close once stable
Alex: closing note: last seen 5xx at 10:13:15 UTC, will reopen if it recurs :eyes:
